note: The `recording` content type, taking the space from 13 types to 14.
AWK-32. Read by migrate_portfolio.py --schema, asserted by
recording-schema.test.ts.
THE FOURTEENTH, not the twelfth. ADR-0012 calls `recording` 'the twelfth
content type in the space' and AWK-31 calls `project`/`imageGroup` 'the
twelfth and thirteenth' — two accepted claims on slot twelve, because both
were written against an 11-type space and neither anticipated the other
landing first. AWK-31 landed on 2026-08-14, so this one is fourteenth.
portfolio-schema.json predicted exactly this; ADR-0012 was corrected under
AWK-32 rather than left to be rediscovered.
Each entry under `fields` is a VERBATIM Contentful field object, so the
applier sends it as-is and never translates. Anything that is not a field
object lives at the group level, outside them. Same convention as
archive-schema.json and portfolio-schema.json.
CREATION, not migration — `recording` has never existed in this space, which
is what makes its FOUR required fields safe (`url`, `label`, `kind`,
`concert`; only `programItem` is optional). The applier will NOT append a
required field to a type that already holds entries; see migrate_portfolio.py.
SINGLE TYPE, so unlike portfolio-schema.json nothing here depends on creation
order. `concert` and `programItem` are named in linkContentType validations
and both have existed since the original import, so there is no ordering
hazard to preserve.
Entries take Contentful's AUTO-GENERATED ids. Recordings are curated by hand
one video at a time (ADR-0012's 'seeding cannot be scripted'), so they need no
prefix convention — same reasoning as `project`, and unlike the archive's
`cnc-`/`pi-` ids which exist only because import_to_contentful.py computes them.

kind: ADR-0012's two values, lowercase. They follow `soloist.instrument`'s
precedent per the record, and they are STORED values a component switches
on — 'is this a video or an audio link' — not display strings, which is why
they are not Title Case like `period` and `forms`.
Both current sources are video (YouTube). `audio` is declared anyway because
the record declares it: the orchestra's SoundCloud exists, and while today's
feed there is a podcast ABOUT the orchestra rather than performance, an
audio-only performance link is the obvious next source and adding a value to
an `in` list means republishing the type.

createTypes.name: Recording
createTypes.description: An outbound link to a recording of one performance, hosted by whoever already publishes it. Never embedded and never self-hosted (ADR-0012). An empty programItem means the recording covers the whole concert.

beyondTheRecord: ONE validation here is not in ADR-0012's schema table, and it is called out
rather than slipped in: `url` carries Contentful's URL regexp alongside
`unique: true`. The record specifies `Symbol, unique` and is silent on format.
Added because this field's ONLY consumer is an <a href>. ADR-0012 ships text
links and nothing else, so a value that is not a URL does not degrade — it
renders a dead link on a Concert page, and the failure appears in the built
page rather than at authoring time. `project.liveUrl` and `project.repoUrl`
already carry this exact pattern, verbatim from a type authored in the
Contentful web app, which is what makes the web app render it as its built-in
URL match rather than an opaque custom regexp.
It is a format check and not an editorial policy, which is the line
portfolio-schema.json drew when it declined to trim RichText marks ADR-0003
SETTLED: Alex confirmed it stays (2026-08-14), so ADR-0012's table reads as a
minimum rather than as an exhaustive list. Left recorded rather than deleted
because the next reader comparing this file to the record will find a
validation the record does not mention, and 'someone decided this' is the
thing they need to know. recording-schema.test.ts pins it either way.

why: THE SIXTH invariant this project cannot express declaratively, after
`sideBySide`'s image cap (ADR-0004), `satOut` ⊆ `program` (ADR-0006),
`(composer, slug)` uniqueness (ADR-0008), `featuredRank`-requires-`body`
(ADR-0003) and the CSP's inline-script hash (ADR-0010).
`recording.programItem` must belong to `recording.concert.program`.
Contentful validates a field against a literal, never against another
field, so both links can be individually valid while the pair is nonsense:
a recording pointing at cnc-20221218 and pi-20200223-3 passes every
validation on this type and asserts that a 2020 Brooklyn Museum performance
happened at a 2022 concert.
That is not a hypothetical shape. It is exactly the error ADR-0012 spends
its longest section preventing — the three 'BSO Mexico 2020' videos whose
works ARE on cnc-20200223's program but whose performance was the Mexico
tour, not the Brooklyn Museum night. The schema cannot tell those two
assignments apart, so the build has to.
ATTRIBUTION, because ADR-0012 and this file appear to disagree. The record
says the invariant 'joins the CI assertion AWK-17 built and proved'. AWK-17
built the harness — scripts/assert-pages.test.ts — and that is where the
check belongs. But it is named AWK-39 here because the check cannot run
until entries are readable through the Delivery API, and no CDA token is
wired up yet; that is AWK-39. Note also that 'CI' is aspirational: there is
no CI in this repo at all (no .github/), so the assertion runs in
`bun run test` and nothing runs it automatically.
It derives from `concert`, and a second copy is a second source of truth to
drift. ADR-0012 states this outright.
Worth stating as an absence rather than an omission because a `date` on the
recording is the FIRST thing a seeder reaches for — the RSS feed hands you a
<published> element per video, and it is the wrong date. The Tchaikovsky
Violin Concerto was published 2023-04-01 for a 2022-12-18 performance, and
the Nimrod from the same concert was published 2023-06-14, nearly six months
out. A `date` field would have quietly captured the publish date on both.
`url` carries the uniqueness and (`concert`, `programItem`) deliberately
does NOT — Contentful could not express a composite constraint anyway, but
the point is that the pair MUST stay non-unique.
One Program Item legitimately holds several recordings. The BSO published
the Tchaikovsky Violin Concerto twice — first movement alone and complete —
and both are pi-20221218-3. Elgar's Wand of Youth is split across two
videos. Movement cuts and complete cuts are genuinely distinct addresses,
